notes.title: D minor vs D major
notes.note: How does he get away with both D minor (bars 2.3 and 10.3, and again in bars 18 to 21) and D major (bars 6.3 and 14.3) in the same song? Come back to this after finishing the chords for the whole album.
E’s are on-beat sixteenths, unresolved whether they color it as maj7.

Kept as one G7 span. Bass circles D and G, pulse2 sits on D and F. The B only visits the bass for two notes (23.3), too brief to change the label. Could be heard as G sus until the B arrives, but I read it as G7 throughout: the composer wanted the B and it just didn't fit the melody and pulse2 already written, so it only got in there.

C7, bringing us home to F. Bass has two roles: the upper voice alternates G and Bb (fifth and flat seventh), the lower voice walks C, D, Eb, E (root up to the third; the D and Eb are only steps on the way, not chord tones). Melody has G then Bb, pulse2 holds G the whole time. The bass ends on E and the loop lands on F, a leading tone pulling home. The A before the Bb in the melody is an approach note, not a leading tone, but it acts like one: A, Bb, then the loop lands on C at 1.3, so the melody also climbs by step back into the start.
